checks.claim: C1: The family uses the same general nonnegative smooth compact psi, the original d1 fractional-time Riesz/white covariance with its amplitude, and the actual F with both entries and constants.
checks.reason: Target lines 9-34 match tilt Section 1 and local-flow Section 4. With extension by zero and Fubini, h_sigma=Gamma*q_sigma equals tilt (5) at t=sigma. Tilt Section 3 assumes only real psi, not separability. The covariance notation is explicitly distributional shorthand. The equation (w,v_xx+h v) has the attractive sign of u_tt=u_xx+h u, and the coefficient-1 retained potential agrees with tilt Section 5.

checks.claim: C1: q_sigma is smooth, compact, commonly supported and >=q_avg>=0 nonzero, and h_sigma>=Gamma*q_avg, with C1, time, tail and derivative regularity available.
checks.reason: For sigma,u in [0,1], |sigma-u|<=1 and a>0 give kernel >=1, so q_sigma>=q_avg. The positivity sets {q_sigma>0} and {q_avg>0} coincide, so the supports are literally identical. Differentiation under the integrable kernel gives smoothness. A positive Radon convolution preserves the order. Tilt (6) gives Lipschitz dependence into C_b^1 and a uniform W1,infinity tail. The all-derivative boundedness prose in tilt Section 3 covers the higher spatial derivatives used for fixed-member classical solutions.

checks.claim: C1: sigma is an index and not an amplitude, sigma=0 is allowed with a nonzero potential, and no b0>0 assumption is made on sigma.
checks.reason: Target lines 20-23 and 96 say this explicitly. At sigma=0, q_0>=q_avg is nonzero.

checks.claim: C2: Old fixed-q results can be legally instantiated at each q_sigma with coupling 1, and they confer only pointwise facts.
checks.reason: Each q_sigma is a legal nonzero nonnegative smooth compact q, and K containing 1 is a legal interval in the ground, weighted and complement notes. Target lines 36-42 and input-map lines 10-18 and 30-37 disclaim common constants over varying q. The accepted notes' constants depend on the fixed U, so they do not restate S1-S3. The optional temporal-range convention is not needed by S1-S3 and could not be checked against target-v2, which is outside the packet (see minors).

checks.claim: C2: S1 is well posed and feasible as a new deduction, with no global L1 Riesz assumption and no simplicity-before-existence circularity.
checks.reason: A fixed trial w_L with h_sigma>=U_avg gives E1(sigma)<=-epsilon using only a local mass of U_avg. Boundedness gives a uniform lower bound. The T10.2 and p140 essential-spectrum definition then give an isolated eigenvalue before the conditional T10.13 is used. Lipschitz potential dependence and common max-min classes make E1 and E2 Lipschitz through threshold 0. Compactness of [0,1] gives Delta>0 and rate separation. Infinitely many Riesz bound states are allowed. This is a feasibility assessment, not proof acceptance.

checks.claim: C2: The exact Teschl second-edition statements match their claimed use.
checks.reason: Title and copyright pages show Second Edition, GSM 157, ISBN 978-1-4704-1704-8, copyright 2009, 2014. Lemma 7.21 on pp200-201 defines bounded Borel functions vanishing at infinity. T10.2 on p258 gives self-adjointness on H2, lower boundedness, essential spectrum [0,infinity) and a C_c^infinity core. T10.13 on p273 is conditional on the bottom being an eigenvalue. p140 gives the essential-spectrum definition, (4.37) and the threshold convention. T4.12 on p141 gives max-min, followed by the form-domain sentence. Page headers agree with the custody JSON's 12-page offset.

checks.claim: C3: The weighted p, p', p'' bounds, duality norms, projection algebra, continuity, entrance and commutation in S2 are correct and feasible for the real family.
checks.reason: Uniform lambda bounds, a uniform h bound and a uniform tail allow one exterior comparison radius and rate. e=(p,lambda p) and ell=(<p,v>+<p,w>/lambda)/2 give ell(e)=1 and ell(p,-lambda p)=0. ell(e0)=(1/2)integral p is uniformly positive. Positive overlap plus the gap gives Lipschitz H2 dependence, and the local-tail split gives operator-norm continuity. Time-constant h_sigma satisfies local-flow (5.6) with zero constant part. Commutation extends from compact-plus-constant phases by the defining density, with no compact-only density, point evaluation or E-density shortcut.

checks.claim: C3: The positive smooth averaged-observable clause in S2 is a fully specified statement.
checks.reason: Target line 72 requires J_phi bounded on F and inf_sigma J_phi(e_sigma)>0, but J_phi is defined nowhere in the target or the packet. An exact search finds only target line 72. Tilt has a different squared flow functional J_delta (line 254) and a displacement functional ell_phi (line 256). The clause therefore leaves open a linear first-entry pairing, a squared functional (not a bounded linear functional in the same sense), or a velocity-inclusive functional. Under the first-entry reading the claim looks feasible because p_sigma>0 is continuous in H2 over compact [0,1], but the review may not supply that definition and PASS the original.

checks.claim: C4: S3 is a true-looking, feasible obligation stating a uniform F complement for all sigma in [0,1], tau>=0 from derived data, with no assumed uniformity or hidden conclusion.
checks.reason: With M=sup||h_sigma||, c=1+M and A_sigma=H_sigma+c, one has B<=A_sigma<=cB, so the fractional identification is uniform. The Q-phase entries, threshold-zero case and decaying branch carry over. Finite propagation and identity (9) apply to frozen h_sigma, and the tail product gives C exp(-beta tau) using the uniform weighted constants from S2. Target lines 80-84 require fractional calculus and localized tails with nonlocal growth, and forbid inference from per-member estimates. Local-flow and complement-note obligations are mapped in input-map lines 30-37. This is feasibility only, not a proof.

checks.claim: C5: The analytic white two-bump witness refutes a universal exact h_sigma=b(sigma)U representation.
checks.reason: Independently verified. f1 supported in (1/8,1/4) and f2(u)=f1(1-u) supported in (3/4,7/8) give a legal nonnegative test in C_c^infinity((0,1)xR). The substitution gives int u^-a f2=B and int (1-u)^-a f2=A, so h_0=c(Aq1+Bq2) and h_1=c(Bq1+Aq2). A>B>0 follows from u<1-u on supp f1, a>0, and f1 positive on an open interval. Disjoint bumps give determinant c^2(A^2-B^2)q1(x1)q2(x2)>0, while any b(sigma)U has determinant 0, including the case where a value of b vanishes. Disjoint time supports and spatial bumps also rule out a single product form of psi. White with a<1 is inside the original model.

major: Target S2 line 72 uses an undefined functional J_phi, so its 'bounded on F' and 'inf_sigma J_phi(e_sigma)>0' obligations are not frozen. The packet's closest objects are the squared J_delta and the displacement pairing ell_phi. The actual functional must be fixed before long proof, because linear versus squared and displacement versus velocity-inclusive readings have different meanings and consumers.
minor: S3 does not spell out the quantifiers. A clearer wording is: there exist C finite and eta in (0,inf_sigma lambda_sigma), independent of sigma and tau. The heading's 'uniform' and the S2 analogue make the intended reading clear.

S1 uses L for the upper spectral rate, while tilt uses L=1/delta for the fast horizon. Earlier adjudications already warned about this kind of symbol collision, and later consumers should keep the two apart.

Input-map line 14 says 'nonnegative auxiliary smooth f in (0,1)' without saying nonzero or compactly supported, although positivity and boundedness of k_f require both. k_f and the older application-range condition are not defined in the frozen packet. This clause is optional and is not load-bearing for S1-S3.
The target does not explicitly record that signed or otherwise non-positive psi remain outside this family. It makes no contrary claim, and 'general class' is only implicitly deferred by line 97.

The diagnostics' determinant suppresses the q1(x1)q2(x2) factor and hard-codes not_proportional after an assertion. The non-detecting control is a literal identity and has no JSON row. This is acceptable given the stated scope, but it adds no evidence about the integrals.

Target line 88 says the witness 'rules out' the representation, while falsification-v1.md is labelled a candidate not yet adopted. This review supports the witness on its own scope, but adoption remains a separate act.

required_repairs: Define J_phi explicitly in the S2 statement, including whether it is linear or squared and which phase entries it pairs, using the local duality on F with no point evaluation. Then re-audit the revised statement.
limitations: Assessment of S1-S3 covers statement, fidelity and feasibility only. None of S1-S3 is proved or accepted here. Only the short witness was assessed as a proof, on its own scope.
